decisions.reason: The C4 definition supplies continuous coordinate partials but not total derivatives. Added the existing continuous-partials theorem to F1 and deps: applying it to gradient-coordinate partials through order two licenses the repeated line chain rule. The two scalar Taylor remainders give sqrt(d) M4 epsilon^2/6, and the two evaluation errors give eta/epsilon. Statement unchanged; no propagation.

Finite supplied coordinates do not prevent nonfinite length sums in the numerical procedure. Added a before-use check for every arithmetic/norm result, including cumulative lengths, targets and interpolated images, and a strict cumulative-length check before segment lookup. Zero chords, domain checks, tolerance-before-budget ordering and exact redistribution are preserved. Exact finite samples in all four direct item consumers retain the same procedure.

The locator separates the paper’s first-order-saddle motivation from the format “defined here”, meaning this library item. Read the complete cited §I (pp. 9901–9902): it discusses the negative-curvature direction, not interval validation. The Definition explicitly adopts the certificate as input and disclaims any eigensolver guarantee; the spectral theorem licenses its ordered real eigenvalues. There is no mathematical or provenance claim that the paper supplies interval certification, so no edit is warranted.

F1 incorrectly attributed unit speed to the MEP definition, although the Statement already assumes unit speed on all J. Reworded F1 to distinguish the definition’s normalized tangent from that assumption. Taylor subtraction gives M3 h^2/6; the unequal-step remainder weights sum to h_minus h_plus, and normalization uses norm at least 1/2 to give the stated factor four. Statement unchanged; focused strict contract passes with zero errors/warnings.

F1 attributed unit derivative to a definition that only normalizes a nonzero derivative. Reworded it to use the explicit unit-speed assumption A1. The chord Taylor expansion has T dot K=0, yielding O(h^3) length error; summing over L/h chords gives O(h^2) cumulative-length error. Linear interpolation and unit speed then give O(h^2) redistribution error, including fixed endpoints. Statement unchanged; focused strict contract passes with zero errors/warnings.

The analytic annular-sector example omitted its prescribed forbidden set. Declared C_bad={(0,0)} and verified the domain excludes it by radius greater than 3/4. The polar chart is smooth with smooth inverse; its orthogonal coordinate directions give zero radial gradient at n=0 and nonzero path speed 2a. The endpoint potential zeros are minima, and the orthogonal critical-point chart gives Hessian eigenvalues -4a^2 and 1. The final string-sampling caveat remains sound after the earlier algorithm repair. No Statement/Definition changed; strict contract passes.

The original inputs did not supply the spectral-data provider needed by step 2. Added an explicit input routine E with a finite success/failure return contract and an explicit call after the gradient/budget checks. Success supplies orthogonal Q, ordered approximate values and validated interval certificates; existing residual, margin, overlap and exact Newton-solve branches remain intact. The direct proposition uses only accepted updates and the same exact Hessian solve, so its mathematical conclusion is unchanged. The owning manifest Definition mirror is synchronized under the shared-write lock.

The mode-angle argument is sound: the HVP bound gives Rayleigh quotient at most -gamma/4 and residual at most tau_rot+delta; all positive eigenmodes are separated from that quotient by at least 5gamma/4. The local root transfer needed an explicit norm convention. Stated induced Euclidean operator Lipschitz continuity in the Statement and A4, so the radius inequality exactly matches the local saddle certificate. Both direct consumers use the angle conclusion only, which is unchanged; the translation theorem already states a vectorwise equivalent operator bound.

The Statement already imports the full mode-bound hypotheses, but F1 incorrectly presents A3 alone as sufficient. Expanded A3 with the full finite-difference segment and force/third-derivative error data, and made F1 also use A2’s enclosure. Added the existing continuous-partials theorem to justify the gradient’s C1 regularity in F5. For F3, interchanging the two endpoints in the Newton-remainder lemma gives the required H_* expansion. The spectral projection denominator is at least 3gamma; reflection isometries then give the stated kappa and geometric noise-floor recurrence. Statement unchanged; focused strict contract passes.

The explicit family R_c proves nonuniqueness, but absent stability hypotheses alone do not prove inaccuracy. Replaced the undefined accuracy inference with an explicit reference calculation: the second midpoint has distance 1 from the straight MEP R_0 despite zero residual; both midpoints still lie on their own exact MEPs. Declared C_bad empty so U=R^2 meets the tube interface. All force/spacing calculations and the title’s nonuniqueness claim are preserved. Proof-only/Example edits leave every Statement/Definition unchanged.
